title: Start with convex hull foundations
description: Begin with the C8 lecture to understand orientation predicates, point ratios, and the first hull algorithms used throughout later topics.

title: Move from polygons to triangulations
description: Study polygon triangulation, art gallery reasoning, then point-set triangulation to see how local geometric predicates scale to structural decompositions.

title: Study proximity structures
description: Use the Voronoi lecture to connect nearest-site regions, Delaunay triangulations, sweep-line events, and DCEL planar subdivision representation.

title: Follow sweep-line intersections
description: Read the intersections lecture to understand event/status structures and output-sensitive detection for segment and polygon intersection problems.

title: Finish with duality and optimization
description: Use the final lecture to connect half-plane intersections, point-line duality, and linear programming formulations in geometry.

title: Practice with seminar sheets
description: Work through Seminar 5 and 6 exercise sheets, then compare against the solution files to consolidate hull, triangulation, and art gallery methods.

title: Check readiness with the exam model
description: Use the model subject to review the full C8-C13/14 spread through multiple-choice and concise open problems.
